Subject: Urgent: temporary burst uplift for launch

Hi Markus,

Quick one — we have a go-live for Aureus Insights on July 20 and expect a concentrated ramp during the first 72 hours. Based on our load tests the inference traffic could spike to ~3x our baseline token volume for short windows (peaks of ~4M tokens/hour). We understand Redwood has burst and fairness policies; given the business impact of missing the launch we wanted to request a short-term uplift to our burst quota and a temporary priority lane for the 48-hour launch period.

Attached is our scaling request (Aureus_Scaling_Request.xlsx) with hourly projections and a brief roll-forward plan. Our asks:
- Temporary burst cap increased from 1.2M tokens/hr -> 4.5M tokens/hr for 48 hours (July 20 00:00 UTC — July 22 00:00 UTC)
- Exemption from fair-share throttling for the same window (so requests don't get deprioritized during global contention)
- A contractual Appendix or short addendum confirming the dates and rollback plan

We can accept additional monitoring, enhanced logging, and a hard failover to a smaller model if needed. Budget for this uplift is available and we can sign a short amendment. Can you confirm feasibility and next steps?

Thanks,
Erin

Subject: Re: Urgent: temporary burst uplift for launch — capacity & safeguards

Markus / team / Erin,

We can support a temporary uplift with the following constraints and safeguards. Summary below — details in attached SLA_Appendix_draft.pdf.

Feasibility: Yes — we have capacity headroom in us-west and us-east GPU fleets for a 48-hour window starting July 20 00:00 UTC.

Recommended uplift terms (engineering):
- Granted soft cap: 4.2M tokens/hr (sustained) with 5.0M tokens/hr short spikes (<= 6 minutes) allowed before automated mitigations kick in.
- Fair-share exemption: We can route Aureus traffic to a temporary priority pool for the window. This pool has preemptive limits to preserve overall platform stability.
- Fallback behavior: If sustained utilization > 85% of the priority pool for >10 minutes, traffic will be throttled to a fallback model (reduced context size) with an immediate alert to Aureus and Redwood on-call.
- Monitoring & telemetry: We’ll enable per-request tracing for the time window and provide a read-only dashboard link.
- Costing: uplift will be billed at 2.5x standard token rate for the uplift window (we can apply a one-time credit if churn/incident occurs).

Operational asks from Aureus (please confirm):
1) Which time zone should we treat as canonical for start/end (we propose UTC).
2) A primary on-call contact during the 48h window and any escalation steps.
3) Agreement to the fallback model if load threatens stability.

Attachment: SLA_Appendix_draft.pdf (PDF, 12KB) — contains wording we can sign quickly to formalize the uplift and rollback clauses.

If everyone OK I’ll set the priority pool and enable telemetry on July 19 for final smoke tests.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
